items.title: Fifth Circuit Rejects "Ghost Rates" in Federal QPA Calculations Under the No Surprises Act - Yahoo Finance
items.reason: This is direct litigation from the Fifth Circuit interpreting a core No Surprises Act mechanism (Qualified Payment Amount/QPA calculations), which directly impacts how out-of-network payment disputes are resolved and affects revenue-cycle operations.
items.summary: The Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals issued a decision rejecting the use of "ghost rates"—rates from providers who are no longer in-network—in calculating the Qualified Payment Amount (QPA) under the No Surprises Act's Independent Dispute Resolution process. This ruling interprets how insurers must determine the federal benchmark rate when adjudicating balance-billing disputes for out-of-network emergency and non-emergency services. The decision clarifies QPA methodology, which directly affects how much providers and payers must pay in IDR disputes and has implications for revenue-cycle teams managing claims and dispute resolutions. This federal appellate interpretation will likely apply across multiple states and influences the calculation methods revenue-cycle teams must use when preparing for or responding to IDR proceedings.

items.title: Cigna faces $13M lawsuit over addiction care billing - BenefitsPRO
items.reason: This is a payer litigation item involving Cigna facing a lawsuit with a specific dollar amount, directly matching the topic's focus on health insurer lawsuits and enforcement actions.
items.summary: Cigna is facing a $13 million lawsuit related to its billing practices for addiction care services. The lawsuit targets the payer's handling of addiction treatment claims, a critical issue for revenue-cycle teams managing behavioral health billing, claims processing, and reimbursement disputes with major insurers. This enforcement action reflects ongoing scrutiny of payer practices around mental health and substance-use disorder coverage, which directly affects provider networks and claim payment policies that revenue-cycle departments must navigate.

items.title: Jack Karns: Medicare Advantage denials draw federal attention - reflector.com
items.reason: The item reports on federal regulatory attention to Medicare Advantage claims denials, which falls directly within CMS/Medicare Advantage enforcement and payer litigation topics relevant to revenue-cycle teams.
items.summary: Federal regulators are focusing attention on Medicare Advantage plan denial practices, according to an opinion piece by Jack Karns in reflector.com. The item indicates that CMS or federal authorities are scrutinizing how Medicare Advantage plans deny claims, a regulatory enforcement action that directly affects provider reimbursement and revenue-cycle operations. This development is significant for revenue-cycle teams because Medicare Advantage denials represent a major source of claim rejections, and federal attention may lead to policy changes or enforcement actions against payers that impact appeal processes and payment timelines.
